title: Degree Bounds for Linearized Permutation Decompositions
summary: Degree-16 factors are not universally sufficient over the 256-element binary field; determine relaxed degree conditions that guarantee low-degree linearized permutation decompositions.

formal_statement.body: Determine conditions on the allowed factor degrees under which a linearized permutation polynomial over $\mathbb{F}_{2^8}$ admits a composition decomposition $L=L_1\circ L_2$ into two low-degree linearized permutation polynomials, and prove existence whenever those conditions hold. Requiring both factors to have degree $2^4$ is not universally sufficient, since some linearized polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_{2^8}$ cannot be decomposed in this way. Relaxing the degree restriction can increase the possibility that suitable permutation-polynomial factors exist, but a theoretical existence proof under relaxed bounds remains to be established.

scope.domain: Finite-field algebra of composition decompositions for linearized permutation polynomials.
parameters: The base field with 2^8 elements, which fixes the finite-field setting
The allowed degrees of the two factors, which govern the sought decomposition
scope.unresolved_remainder: Identify relaxed factor-degree conditions that ensure the decomposition exists and prove existence whenever those conditions hold.
